claims.text: The nanoscale platinum-group catalyst exhibits excellent performance in ethanol oxidation.
The catalyst's ethanol-oxidation performance is governed by dynamic formation of a transient surface oxide layer.
The transient surface oxide facilitates water activation.
The transient surface oxide promotes oxidation of strongly bound carbonaceous intermediates.
The as-synthesized catalyst has a pristine metallic surface.
Mild thermal oxidation in an oxygen-containing atmosphere will pre-form or enrich a small amount of PGM oxide at the catalyst surface.
A transient nanoscale PGM oxide species forms on the catalyst surface.
The controlled surface oxide increases the catalyst's ability to activate water and generate surface OH species.
The generated OH species oxidize strongly adsorbed ethanol-derived intermediates.
Strongly adsorbed ethanol-derived intermediates can poison the catalyst if they are not removed.
The dynamic oxide layer balances adsorption and desorption kinetics, enhancing selectivity, activity, and durability.
Oxidation-pretreated catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation currents than untreated catalysts.
Oxidation-pretreated catalysts will favor more complete ethanol oxidation than untreated catalysts.
Oxidation-pretreated catalysts will retain performance for longer than untreated catalysts.
The proposed mechanism applies under room-temperature acidic electrochemical ethanol-oxidation conditions.
The proposed mechanism may fail at high pH or elevated temperature because surface-oxide dynamics differ in those regimes.
